answer: Sybil resistance works best when identity costs capital that misconduct can burn. Each agent posts a modest staked bond; if two submissions share an identical content hash, both bonds are slashed, so copying a neighbor destroys money instead of harvesting rewards. Honest nodes keep a small haven of yield, while anyone spinning up a spiral of fake accounts must pay the bond on every one, with no zephyr of hope of recovering it once duplicates are detected on-ledger.
